verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'After splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time, ... waters off San Diego'; R2: 'splashed down off the coast of San Diego on April 10 just past 8 p.m. EDT / 5 p.m. PDT'; R3: 'splashdown off the coast of San Diego ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 PDT'; R4: 'safely splashed down at 8:07 p.m. ET'; R5: 'splash down ... at approximately 8:07 p.m. Eastern time ... verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the exact location, date (implied by context and URLs in 2026), and time including ET/PT conversion.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule landed after a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'returned to Earth after 10 days ... Orion “Integrity” spacecraft'; R3: 'ending Artemis II’s historic 10-day mission ... Orion spacecraft has splashed down'; R4: 'ending the record-breaking 10-day mission ... Orion capsule'; R6: 'concluding a monumental and risky 10-day journey ... Orion capsule'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe the Orion capsule's splashdown/landing concluding a 10-day mission.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'After 10 days'; R3: 'ending historic 10-day mission'; R4: 'record-breaking 10-day mission'; R5: 'after 10 days'; R6: '10-day journey ... 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Widely described as a 10-day mission in sources, though precise duration noted as ~9 days 1 hour in some (e.g., R4), but claim matches common phrasing.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission concluded with a fiery reentry and parachute-assisted landing.

verifications.evidence: R1: 'slipped into Earth’s atmosphere at more than 24,000 miles per hour ... heat enveloping ... drogues deployed ... main parachutes'; R3: 'reentry into Earth's atmosphere ... superheated charged particles ... plasma ... deploy parachutes'; R4: 'fiery plunge through Earth's atmosphere ... parachutes have deployed'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe high-speed atmospheric reentry with heat/plasma ('fiery') and parachutes for splashdown landing.

verifications.claim: According to the USAToday splashdown timeline, the crew module separated from the service module at 7:33 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Artemis II splashdown timeline ... 7:33 p.m.: Orion’s crew module will separate from the service module'
verifications.reasoning: R3 is USA Today; timeline exactly matches the time and event.

verifications.claim: According to the USAToday splashdown timeline, the crew module initiated reentry at 7:53 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Artemis II splashdown timeline ... 7:53 p.m.: Orion reaches 400,000 feet ... first contact with the upper atmosphere ... entry interface'
verifications.reasoning: R3 is USA Today; timeline exactly matches reentry initiation/entry interface time.

verifications.claim: According to the USAToday splashdown timeline, the crew module deployed parachutes just before 8:04 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Artemis II splashdown timeline ... 8:03 p.m.: ... drogue parachutes will deploy ... 8:04 p.m.: ... the three main parachutes will deploy'
verifications.reasoning: R3 is USA Today; timeline shows drogue at 8:03 (just before 8:04) and main at 8:04, supporting parachute deployment just before 8:04.
